rows.proposal: Retail and logistics teams need AI and analytics that fit existing data and workflows—not disconnected demos. I’ve shipped real-time object and face detection on RTSP camera feeds, exposed through HTTP services, and built a multi-model inference service for freight-forwarding document workflows. In that logistics deployment, five models were consolidated onto one 24 GB GPU; a client review reported the cloud bill fell by about 40%. For retail analytics, I built a sales-and-returns dashboard that traced a returns issue to sizing-chart errors on 23 product pages; after correction, that supplier’s returns fell to 4%. The weekly report went from five hours of assembly to about ten minutes of review, with metric definitions documented in a data dictionary. For your clients, I’d start by mapping business workflows, available data, existing platforms, and governance constraints. Then I’d recommend targeted ML, NLP, or computer-vision use cases, integration points, and reporting measures. For OpenAI-based solutions, I’d validate data compatibility, access controls, expected scale, and evaluation needs before proposing a platform or production design; I would also define a practical monitoring and maintenance plan. Could we schedule a short discovery call to prioritize one retail and one logistics use case?

rows.proposal: Turning reviews and survey responses into reliable sentiment trends—without losing the reasons behind each score—is the core challenge here. I built a review-analysis solution for a hotel group with 19 properties, fine-tuning a multilingual transformer for aspect-level sentiment on 3,000 team-labeled reviews across eight aspects. For your data, I’d align labels and categories first, then establish a baseline and validate it on a representative held-out sample. I’d break results down by topic, source, and time, and check ambiguous language and class imbalance before treating the output as decision-ready. I can deliver concise trend summaries with examples, caveats, and prioritized recommendations, plus tables suitable for Excel. I’d coordinate interpretation with your stakeholders so recommendations connect to decisions, not just model scores. I also wrote an internal text-classification service used by a support team handling about 9,000 tickets a month, which is relevant to making text analysis useful in an operational setting. Could you share a sample dataset and the decisions you most want the analysis to inform?

compliance.redacted_text: Your digital book needs to become an assistant that answers from the source, reads passages aloud, and supports an avatar without making up content. I’d start with a short technical discovery, then build a Python-based retrieval-augmented system: ingest and section the book, index searchable chunks, and have the chatbot answer from retrieved passages with source references and a clear fallback when the material doesn’t support an answer. Add text-to-speech for read-aloud, then connect an avatar layer chosen around your preferred visual style, latency, and hosting constraints. I’d recommend the model and platform after confirming those constraints rather than defaulting to Watson or TensorFlow without a reason. I’ve also worked on a phone voice-assistant pipeline, profiling transcription, language-model, and speech-synthesis stages to reduce response delay. I can use that background to shape a practical build plan and implementation. My rate is $50/hour. What format is the book in, and do you already have a preferred avatar or deployment platform?

rows.proposal: Preparing for Java interviews means practicing the right problems while learning to explain your reasoning and improve your code under interview constraints. I can structure sessions around that process: start with a short diagnostic problem, identify gaps in the approach, work through a solution step by step, then review complexity, edge cases, and cleaner alternatives. We can tailor the practice plan to your target roles, current comfort level, and interview timeline, and adjust the pace as we go. I want to be transparent: the materials available to me do not verify Java, LeetCode, DSA, or interview-coaching experience, so I won’t present those as established credentials. I would begin by confirming your expectations and using an initial problem to see whether my explanations and feedback are a useful fit. My proposed rate is $55/hour. What Java topic or interview problem would you like to use for a first session?
